title: Artificial intelligence in higher education: the state of the field
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper presents a systematic review of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education from 2016 through 2022. The authors sought to update prior reviews and answer three questions: where the research was conducted, what academic levels and subject domains were studied, and who the intended users were, as well as how AI was being used in higher education settings.

The review included 138 peer-reviewed journal articles identified through database and hand searches, screened using PRISMA procedures. The studies covered six continents, with the largest share from Asia, especially China and Taiwan, and most first authors were affiliated with colleges of education or computer science. Undergraduate students were the dominant population, while graduate students appeared much less often. Common subject domains included language learning, computer science, and engineering, and intended users were mostly students, followed by instructors and managers.

Through grounded coding, the authors identified five major usage categories: assessment/evaluation, predicting, AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, and managing student learning. Across the literature, AI was commonly used for automated assessment and feedback, prediction of academic performance and dropout risk, and adaptive support through chatbots or tutoring systems. The review concludes that AI in higher education is growing rapidly, with new trends emerging after 2020, but that research remains concentrated in high-income countries, undergraduate contexts, and traditional efficiency-oriented uses rather than more transformative applications.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic artificial intelligence applications in higher education, including assessment, prediction, AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, and student learning management.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper systematically reviewed 138 higher-education studies using AI from 2016 to 2022 and coded how AI was used across studies, without focusing on one named product.

findings.finding_summary: Across 138 studies, AI in higher education was most often used for assessment/evaluation, predicting, AI assistant functions, intelligent tutoring systems, and managing student learning. The review reports that AI was used to support writing, feedback, prediction of academic performance, personalized assistance, and learning analytics, but it does not provide pooled effect sizes.
findings.measure: Systematic review coding of AI use cases in higher education studies

findings.finding_summary: In the language-learning subset of studies, AI was commonly used for writing, reading, and vocabulary acquisition. The review notes examples of automated feedback for writing and AI translation support, but no quantitative subgroup effects are reported for literacy outcomes.
findings.measure: Systematic review coding of language learning studies and literacy-related applications

findings.finding_summary: The review found that 72% of studies focused on students, 17% on instructors, and 11% on managers, and it identified managerial uses such as learning analytics, curriculum sequencing, instructional design, and clustering students. These are descriptive findings only, with no pooled estimate of impact.
findings.measure: Systematic review coding of intended users and management-oriented AI uses

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review with transparent PRISMA methods and dual coding, but it synthesizes heterogeneous studies descriptively rather than estimating effects. The evidence is therefore strong for mapping the field, but not for causal impact on outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports important descriptive trends and use cases, but it does not provide effect sizes or outcome magnitudes. As a result, the practical impact is promising but unclear from the evidence reported.
